problems.name: Implement Trie Prefix Tree
problems.question: Design a trie that supports inserting words, searching complete words, and checking whether any word starts with a given prefix.
problems.constraints: 1 <= word.length, prefix.length <= 2000; calls contain lowercase English letters; at most 30000 operations.

examples.explanation: app is only a prefix until it is inserted.
The terminal flag is set on the app node.
The first character path is missing.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(L) per operation; Space O(total characters). Each character moves one trie edge.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(L) per operation; Space O(L) call stack. Recursive helpers process one character per call.

problems.name: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
problems.question: Design a data structure that adds lowercase words and searches words where dot can match any one letter.
problems.constraints: 1 <= word.length <= 25; calls contain lowercase letters and dots in search; at most 10000 calls.

examples.explanation: No stored word matches pad.
The dot can match b or d.
Both dots match the remaining letters of bad.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time add O(L), search O(26^d * L) worst case where d is wildcard count; Space O(total characters).
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time add O(L), search O(26^d * L); Space O(L) call stack for one search path.

source.label: Design Add and Search Words - LeetCode 211

problems.name: Word Search II
problems.question: Given a board of letters and a list of words, return every word that can be formed by adjacent horizontal or vertical cells without reusing a cell.
problems.constraints: 1 <= board rows, cols <= 12; 1 <= words.length <= 30000; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Only oath and eat can be formed on valid adjacent paths.
The path would need to reuse b.
The single cell forms the word.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn * 4^L) with prefix pruning; Space O(total word characters). Trie nodes cut dead paths early.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn * 4^L) with trie pruning; Space O(total word characters + L) including recursion stack.

problems.name: Replace Words
problems.question: Given dictionary roots and a sentence, replace each word with the shortest root that is its prefix when such a root exists.
problems.constraints: 1 <= dictionary.length <= 1000; 1 <= sentence.length <= 100000; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.input: dictionary = ["cat","bat","rat"], sentence = "the cattle was rattled by the battery"
examples.output: "the cat was rat by the bat"
examples.explanation: cattle, rattled, and battery use their shortest roots.
The shortest root a wins each time.
No word has x as a prefix.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(total root chars + sentence chars); Space O(total root chars). Trie lookup stops at shortest terminal root.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(total root chars + sentence chars); Space O(total root chars + L) including recursion stack.

problems.name: Map Sum Pairs
problems.question: Design a structure that inserts key-value pairs and returns the sum of values of all keys with a given prefix.
problems.constraints: 1 <= key.length, prefix.length <= 50; 1 <= val <= 1000; at most 50 operations in the original problem.

examples.explanation: apple contributes 3 to prefix ap.
apple and app both match ap.
Overwriting apple changes its contribution from 3 to 2.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time insert O(L), sum O(P); Space O(total key chars). Each trie node stores the aggregate prefix sum.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time insert O(L), sum O(P); Space O(L) call stack for update and lookup.

problems.name: Longest Word in Dictionary
problems.question: Given a list of words, return the longest word that can be built one character at a time by other words in the list. Return the lexicographically smallest answer on ties.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 1000; 1 <= words[i].length <= 30; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Every prefix of world is present.
apple and apply have length 5; apple is lexicographically smaller.
No word can be built from single-character prefixes.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL + nodes); Space O(nL). Trie DFS visits only terminal-prefix paths.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(nL + nodes); Space O(nL + L). Recursive DFS builds candidates through terminal nodes.

problems.name: Stream of Characters
problems.question: Design a stream checker that receives one character at a time and returns true if any suffix of the stream equals a dictionary word.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 2000; 1 <= words[i].length <= 200; at most 40000 query calls.

examples.explanation: The suffix cd appears after reading d.
The single-character word f matches the latest suffix.
The suffix kl matches after reading l.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(max word length) per query; Space O(total word chars + max word length). Reverse trie stops at first broken suffix.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(max word length) per query; Space O(total word chars + max word length) including recursion.

problems.name: Search Suggestions System
problems.question: Given product names and a search word, return up to three lexicographically smallest product suggestions after each typed character.
problems.constraints: 1 <= products.length <= 1000; 1 <= products[i].length, searchWord.length <= 3000 total input size.

examples.explanation: Suggestions shrink as the prefix becomes more specific.
The only product matches every prefix.
Each prefix returns up to three sorted matches.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL log n + S); Space O(nL). Trie nodes store at most three sorted suggestions while inserting sorted products.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(nL + S * nodes under prefix); Space O(nL + L). DFS collects up to three words from each prefix node.

problems.name: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
problems.question: Given an integer array, return the maximum XOR value of any two numbers in the array.

examples.explanation: 5 XOR 25 equals 28.
Only one number exists.
The best pair creates all seven lower bits as 1.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(31n); Space O(31n). Each number inserts and queries one path in a binary trie.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(31n); Space O(31n + 31). Recursive insert/query processes one bit per call.

source.label: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers - LeetCode 421

problems.name: Palindrome Pairs
problems.question: Given unique words, return all index pairs [i, j] such that words[i] + words[j] is a palindrome.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 5000; 0 <= words[i].length <= 300; words are unique lowercase strings.

examples.explanation: Each listed concatenation is a palindrome.
bat+tab and tab+bat are palindromes.
The empty string pairs with any palindrome word.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL^2); Space O(nL). Reversed trie stores palindrome suffix candidates.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(nL^2); Space O(nL + L). Recursive insertion and search process one character at a time.

problems.name: Concatenated Words
problems.question: Given an array of words, return all words that are formed by concatenating at least two shorter words from the same array.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 10000; 0 <= words[i].length <= 30; lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Each returned word is composed from shorter dictionary words.
catdog is cat + dog.
aa is a+a and aaa can be a+aa.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL^2); Space O(nL + L). Trie DP follows only dictionary prefixes.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(nL^2); Space O(nL + L). Memoized recursive trie segmentation stores start positions.

problems.name: Word Squares
problems.question: Given same-length words, return all word squares where the kth row and kth column read the same string.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 1000; 1 <= words[i].length <= 5 in the original problem; words contain lowercase letters.

examples.explanation: Rows and columns match for both squares.
The prefix trie finds valid row candidates.
A one-letter word forms a one-row square.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(number of partial squares * candidate lookup); Space O(nk). Trie prefix lookup prunes invalid branches.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(number of partial squares * candidate lookup); Space O(nk + k). Recursive backtracking stores current square.

problems.name: Index Pairs of a String
problems.question: Given a text and a list of words, return all index pairs [i, j] where text substring i..j appears in words.
problems.constraints: 1 <= text.length <= 100; 1 <= words.length <= 20; words and text contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: All matching substrings are returned in sorted order.
Matches can overlap.
No dictionary word appears.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * maxWordLength); Space O(total word chars + P). Trie walk stops when the prefix fails.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * maxWordLength); Space O(total word chars + maxWordLength + P). Recursive scan follows one path per start.

source.label: Index Pairs of a String - LeetCode 1065

problems.name: Prefix and Suffix Search
problems.question: Design WordFilter so f(prefix, suffix) returns the largest index of a word that starts with prefix and ends with suffix.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 15000; 1 <= words[i].length <= 10; at most 15000 queries.

examples.explanation: apple starts with a and ends with e.
apply is the latest matching word.
No word has both constraints.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time constructor O(nL^2), query O(P + S); Space O(nL^2). Combined trie stores every suffix separator word path.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time constructor O(nL^2), query O(P + S); Space O(nL^2 + L). Recursive trie insert/find follows combined keys.

problems.name: Implement Magic Dictionary
problems.question: Design a dictionary that supports building from words and searching whether a query can match a dictionary word after modifying exactly one character.
problems.constraints: 1 <= dictionary.length <= 100; 1 <= word.length <= 100; searchWord contains lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Exactly one character must change.
Changing e to h gives hello.
Length must stay the same.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time build O(nL), search O(26L) worst case; Space O(nL). Trie state tracks whether the modification was used.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time build O(nL), search O(26L) worst case; Space O(nL + L). Recursive DFS tracks mismatch count.

problems.name: Count Pairs With XOR in a Range
problems.question: Given nums, low, and high, count pairs i < j whose XOR value lies in the inclusive range [low, high].

examples.explanation: Six index pairs have XOR in the target range.
Eight pairs satisfy the inclusive range.
No pair exists.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(15n); Space O(15n). Binary trie counts prior values with XOR below each bound.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(15n); Space O(15n + 15). Recursive query processes one bit per level.

source.label: Count Pairs With XOR in a Range - LeetCode 1803

problems.name: Sum of Prefix Scores of Strings
problems.question: For each word, return the sum of counts of all its non-empty prefixes across the entire words array.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 1000; 1 <= words[i].length <= 1000; total characters <= 1000000.

examples.explanation: abc has prefix counts a=2, ab=2, abc=1 for total 5.
Each of its four prefixes appears once.
The prefix a appears twice.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(total characters); Space O(total characters). Trie nodes store prefix frequencies.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(total characters); Space O(total characters + L). Recursive insert and score walk one character per level.

source.label: Sum of Prefix Scores of Strings - LeetCode 2416

problems.name: Short Encoding of Words
problems.question: Given words, return the length of the shortest reference string that encodes every word as a suffix followed by #.
problems.constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 2000; 1 <= words[i].length <= 7; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: time#bell# encodes me because me is a suffix of time.
The encoding is t#.
time# also covers me and ime.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL); Space O(nL). Reverse trie counts only terminal leaves.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(nL); Space O(nL + L). Recursive trie traversal sums leaf depths.

problems.name: Word Break with Trie
problems.question: Given a string and a dictionary, return true if the string can be segmented into one or more dictionary words.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 300; 1 <= wordDict.length <= 1000; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: leetcode splits into leet + code.
Dictionary words may be reused.
No complete segmentation covers the string.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(nL); Space O(total word chars + n). Trie walk from reachable starts avoids unrelated dictionary words.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(nL); Space O(total word chars + n). Memoized recursion stores failed start positions.

problems.name: Design Search Autocomplete System
problems.question: Design an autocomplete system that returns the top three historical sentences for the current typed prefix, ranked by frequency then lexicographic order. Character # commits the current sentence.
problems.constraints: Sentences contain lowercase letters and spaces; times are positive; input is one lowercase letter, space, or #.

examples.input: sentences = ["i love you","island","iroman","i love leetcode"], times = [5,3,2,2], input("i")
examples.explanation: Top matches are ranked by count then lexicographic order.
The prefix becomes "i ".
The current sentence is committed and the buffer resets.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(P + K log K) per query where K is candidates at the prefix; Space O(total sentence characters * prefix maps).
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(P + K log K) per query; Space O(total sentence characters + recursion depth). DFS collects candidates below the prefix node.
